answers.answer: Shuffle all four Conflict III cards and put all four face down at the bottom; shuffle the nine II cards and deal five face down above them; shuffle the three I cards and deal one face down on top. Return unused I and II cards to the box unseen.
answers.evidence: “Shuffle the four Conflict III cards… Shuffle the nine Conflict II cards and deal five… Shuffle the three Conflict I cards and deal one… Return the unused Conflict cards… without looking at them.”

answers.answer: In four-player play a human starts at 1 VP; in three-player play the score starts at 0 VP. In either case the human has two Agents on the Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board; has 12 troops total, with 3 in the garrison and 9 in supply; and takes 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup: score marker on 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0; two Agents on Leader, third Agent is Swordmaster; “three” troops in garrison and “remaining nine” in supply; “Take 1 water.”

answers.answer: Yes, you may take a Reveal turn while Agents remain, but after Revealing your turns are skipped for the rest of that phase, so you cannot later take an Agent turn that round. Only cards remaining in hand are revealed and supply Reveal effects; cards used on Agent turns do not supply Reveal effects. At Clean Up, all cards in front of you from both Agent and Reveal turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: “Agent turns are optional; you may take a Reveal turn while you still have Agents. Once you've taken a Reveal turn, your turns are skipped”; Resolve “just-revealed cards only”; Clean Up moves “all cards in front of you (from your Agent and Reveal turns) to your discard pile.”

answers.answer: A Plot Intrigue played before placing the Agent may grant resources that join your supply and pay the entry cost. Effects from the Agent card played for placement or from the destination happen after entry is paid and cannot pay that same cost. One card can send only one Agent, using only one of its matching Agent icons. A card with no Agent icons cannot be used on an Agent turn; it can only be revealed.
answers.evidence: Plot before placement: “resources it grants before entry join your available supply”; gains “only after placement… cannot pay for that same entry.” “You choose only one Agent icon”; “A card with no Agent icons… only… Reveal turn.”

answers.answer: At a Combat space, all three troops recruited during this turn can deploy, plus up to two more from the garrison: 5 total in this example. At a non-Combat space, normal deployment is not allowed. Recruited troops come from your supply and are placed in the garrison until deployment; an empty supply prevents recruiting more.
answers.evidence: At a Combat space, deploy “any or all units recruited during your current turn… plus up to two more units from your garrison”; cube recruits from supply into garrison.

answers.answer: The Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to any board space connected to an observation post where you have a Spy; you do not recall that Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy from a connected post to bypass another player's Agent at that space, not your own Agent. Gather Intelligence recalls a Spy from a connected post to draw a card; choose it immediately after placing your Agent and before any space or Agent-card effects. One Spy cannot pay for both on the same placement, though two different Spies can pay for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence respectively.
answers.evidence: Spy Agent icon permits a connected space and “you do not recall the Spy”; Infiltrate ignores “another player's Agent”; Gather is chosen “immediately after placing your Agent”; cannot recall “the same Spy to both.”

answers.answer: Two troops give 4 strength, one sandworm gives 3, and four revealed swords give 4, totaling 11. If your last unit is removed, your strength becomes 0. With no unit in the Conflict you cannot participate in Combat Intrigue, since only players with at least one unit may play it.
answers.evidence: “Each troop… 2 strength; each sandworm = 3… each sword… = 1”; if last unit removed “strength becomes 0”; Combat Intrigue begins with players having “at least one unit in the Conflict.”

answers.answer: Yes. Passing does not bar you from acting again after an opponent plays; the window closes after all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to each player's supply (not garrison), sandworms return to the bank, and Combat markers reset to 0.
answers.evidence: “You are not required to pass just because you passed earlier”; resolve after players “pass consecutively”; cleanup returns troops to “supply,” sandworms “to the bank,” and markers reset to 0.

answers.answer: With exactly two tied for first in four-player play, both take the second reward; the remaining players compete for the third reward, but nobody wins the Conflict or takes its card. With the same tie in a three-player game, both tied players take second and no other rewards are given; nobody takes the card. A player at 0 strength receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Tie for first: each gains second and “no one wins the Conflict or takes the Conflict card”; in four players, exactly two tied first leaves others competing for third; “A player with 0 strength receives no reward.”

answers.answer: One or more sandworms double the reward; multiple sandworms do not multiply it further, so two worms do not quadruple rewards. Control of a location and battle icons on a won Conflict card cannot be doubled. For an optional reward of 3 spice for 1 VP, the doubled reward lets you pay 3 spice once for 1 VP or pay 6 spice to gain 2 VP.
answers.evidence: “if you have one or more sandworms… double”; control and Conflict-card battle icons cannot; the example says “pay 3 spice to gain 1 VP, or 6 spice to gain 2.”

answers.answer: After you win a Conflict and take its card face up into your supply, check for a matching battle icon among your other face-up Conflict or Objective cards. If there is a match, you must flip the pair face down and gain 1 VP. In the Endgame, a wild battle icon may match any one of the three icon types in your supply, flipping the pair for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Winner: take won card face up, “Then check that new card”; match with another face-up Conflict or Objective is mandatory; Endgame wild icon matches any of the three.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; falling below 2 loses that VP, and reaching 2 again earns it again. At 4 Influence, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained if you later fall below 4 and earned again on returning to 4. The first player to 4 also gets the Alliance token and its 1 VP; tying the holder at 4 does not take it—an opponent must rise above the holder (or a separate FAQ holder-Influence-loss trigger applies). The token's VP follows its holder.
answers.evidence: At 2, “gain 1 VP; lose it below 2 and regain it”; at 4, track bonus is kept below 4; first to 4 gets Alliance +1 VP; “tying the current holder does not steal the Alliance; rising above… transfers.”

answers.answer: During your Reveal turn you may spend Persuasion before, between, or after Reveal effects. You may pool Persuasion from multiple sources for one purchase and split a source among different purchases. The Imperium Row stays at five cards, replacing a purchased card from the deck, so you may buy its replacement immediately if you can afford it. An acquired card goes face up into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Persuasion may be used “before, between, or after” effects; may pool or split; Row “must always have five cards”; acquired card goes “face up into your discard pile.”

answers.answer: At Makers-phase end, each Agent-free Maker space gets 1 spice added to its bonus-spice spot; visiting a Maker space gains all bonus spice there even when choosing worms. Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Hooks, two worms; Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one worm. Hooks are required only when the summoning effect specifies them and are retained, not spent. While the Shield Wall remains, worms cannot be summoned to Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin; when summoned they go directly to the Conflict, never a garrison.
answers.evidence: Maker phase adds spice when no Agent; visiting gives “all the bonus spice”; Deep Desert/Hagga choices and costs; Hooks are “not spent”; Shield Wall blocks three named Conflicts; worm “immediately deploys” and “can never be placed in a garrison.”

answers.answer: At Recall, if any player has at least 10 VP or the Conflict Deck is empty, Endgame is triggered. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigues, then compare VP. The tiebreakers are spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: “At the end of a round” at 10+ VP or empty Conflict Deck triggers; first resolve Endgame Intrigue; tiebreakers “amount of spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops.”

answers.answer: For standard CHOAM, shuffle all 20 standard contracts face down, reveal two face up on the board, and put the remaining 18 face down in the bank. Add four CHOAM Intrigue cards and four CHOAM Imperium cards to their respective decks. Shaddam is an optional Leader, not compulsory. The 10 contrasting-back contracts are for Rise of Ix compatibility and stay in the box, not part of standard CHOAM.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup: “20 contracts… flip two… remaining 18”; shuffle 4 additional Intrigue and 4 Imperium; Shaddam “option”; contrasting-back set is “used only with Rise of Ix.”

answers.answer: With CHOAM, the contract icon lets you take one of the two face-up contracts into your supply and replace it with a face-up contract from the bank; if no contracts remain, it instead gives 2 Solari. Complete Harvest by visiting a Maker space and gaining the shown spice amount during that turn in total from all sources; complete Immediate as soon as taken; complete Acquire The Spice Must Flow when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: Contract icon: take one face-up and replace from bank; if all taken it “reverts to giving 2 Solari”; Harvest, Immediate, and Acquire The Spice Must Flow conditions are listed.

answers.answer: No. A space contract acquired after you already sent an Agent there cannot be completed on that same turn; you must have held it when sending the Agent. On completion, announce it, gain the shown rewards, then flip it face down and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: If you take a contract for a space “where you've already sent your Agent this turn,” wait until a future turn; must have had contract at placement. Completion: “announce it, gain the rewards… flip it face down and leave it in your supply.”

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival as the third competitor. It gets the Ornithopter Objective. Humans get the other two eligible Objectives, and the human with the First Player marker shown on their Objective starts. The Rival is considered immediately clockwise from First Player, so order is First Player → Rival → other human. The Rival never Reveals.
answers.evidence: “one shared scoring Rival”; “Give the Rival the Ornithopter Objective”; First Player goes to human whose card shows it; order stated; “The Rival never Reveals.”

answers.answer: For an occupied indicated destination, ignore it and reveal another Hagal card. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: place at an eligible empty specified post if available (otherwise ignore placement), then reveal another card and continue the same Agent turn. The Rival ignores ordinary space costs and effects, applying only Hagal effects. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle it and continue.
answers.evidence: “Ignore an occupied destination and reveal again”; Place Spy “do[es] not place an Agent”; reveal another card; “Ignore normal space costs and effects”; empty deck or Reshuffle means reshuffle and continue.

answers.answer: For three or four players, omit Objectives marked for a different player count, shuffle the eligible cards, and deal one random face-up Objective to each human; the player whose card shows the First Player marker starts. Shaddam cannot be used without CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Setup omits mismatched Objective cards and distributes one “random Objective face up”; Shaddam: “Do not use… unless playing with the CHOAM Module.”

answers.answer: The bank's resources and sandworms are not meant to be limited; make any convenient substitution if they run out. By contrast, if your personal troop supply is empty, you cannot recruit more until troops return there. Payments of Solari, spice, or water go back to the bank.
answers.evidence: Bank tokens “are not meant to be limited — make any convenient substitution”; no troops in supply means “you can't recruit more”; payments return to the bank.

answers.answer: The five phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. Round Start reveals a Conflict card first, then each player draws five cards. If Endgame is not triggered at Recall, recall Agents to Leaders, pass First Player clockwise, and begin a new round with Round Start.
answers.evidence: Round order is listed; Round Start: reveal a new Conflict and “Then each player draws five”; Recall if no winner: “recall their Agents… pass the First Player marker clockwise.”

answers.answer: Yes. After paying any entry cost and meeting requirements, board-space effects and Agent-box effects may be carried out in any order; the Faction-space Influence advance is part of those effects. No: entry cost and requirements must be satisfied before resolving any space or Agent-card effects, so Influence from that visit cannot qualify you to enter.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: “must pay any costs and meet any requirements… before resolving any effects”; then space/card effects and Faction advance “in any order.”

answers.answer: An optional arrow cost/effect may be used only once per turn, so you cannot pay it twice on one Agent turn. Most card and space effects are mandatory unless marked “may,” an optional arrow, or optional black-X trash; a direct instruction to trash itself is mandatory. Intrigue conditions and costs must be met to play it.
answers.evidence: Arrow costs/effects “only once per turn,” with only doubled Conflict rewards as exception; FAQ: most effects mandatory; listed exceptions; Intrigue conditions and costs must be met.

answers.answer: A Spy placement icon lets you place a Spy from supply on an unoccupied observation post. If you have no Spies in supply, you may first recall one of your Spies for no effect. If an effect specifies an Agent-icon type connected to the post, the post must meet that specification; otherwise you cannot place there.
answers.evidence: Spy icon places a Spy on an “unoccupied observation post”; if none in supply, “may first recall one… for no effect”; some effects specify an Agent icon that must connect to the post.

answers.answer: No, Infiltrate only bypasses another player's Agent, not your own. Recalling a Spy still requires playing a card for the Agent turn; it does not by itself let you take an Agent turn. You cannot use two Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on one placement, although one may Infiltrate while another gathers Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Infiltrate cannot bypass “your own Agent”; FAQ says recalling a Spy “still requires playing a card for the Agent turn”; cannot recall two for Gather Intelligence on same placement.

answers.answer: At each controlled critical location, the controller gets its visit bonus whenever any player, including that controller, sends an Agent there: Arrakeen and Spice Refinery give 1 Solari; Imperial Basin gives 1 spice. The winner of a Conflict for that location gains control by placing a Control marker on its flag, replacing an opponent marker. When its Conflict is revealed, the existing controller may deploy one troop directly from supply to the Conflict without visiting.
answers.evidence: Winning a critical-location Conflict: place a Control marker, replacing any opponent marker; controlled bonus applies whenever any player visits; reveal triggers optional troop from supply.

answers.answer: For a tie for second, each tied player gets the third reward; the Conflict winner keeps first reward and the card, and no further rewards are given. Tied third-place players get nothing. If three players tie for first, each gets the second reward, nobody takes the card, and no one else gets a reward in either three- or four-player play.
answers.evidence: Tie rules table: second tied each third, winner keeps first and card; third tied get nothing; three tied first get second and “no other rewards in either a three-player or four-player game.”

answers.answer: In a three-player Conflict with three different positive strengths, first and second place receive their printed rewards; third receives nothing. This is also true in a two-human game with a Rival: the Rival counts as the third competitor, and ordinary first and second are rewarded while an untied third is not.
answers.evidence: “with 2 or 3 players (including two humans plus a Rival), ordinary first and second place receive rewards, and ordinary third… nothing.”

answers.answer: Plot Intrigues may be played on your own Agent or Reveal turns; Combat Intrigues only during Combat; Endgame Intrigues only at game end. Keep unplayed Intrigues face down, separate from your deck, and reveal only when played; after resolution put them face up in an Intrigue discard pile. If the Intrigue Deck runs out, shuffle its discard pile into a new deck.
answers.evidence: Intrigue section lists timing by type and storage/discard; FAQ: if Intrigue deck runs out, “shuffle its discard to form a new deck.”

answers.answer: No, an ordinary discard instruction cannot discard an Intrigue unless it says so. An ordinary discard is a card of your choice from your hand, not a card in play or discard pile. Secrets steals one Intrigue chosen at random from each opponent who has at least four Intrigues.
answers.evidence: Discarding: choose a card “from your hand”; “It cannot be an Intrigue card unless specified”; Secrets: each opponent with 4+ gives one “selected at random.”

answers.answer: Trash effects can remove cards from your hand, discard pile, or in play; ordinary trashed cards go to the box, while Reserve cards return to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it pays a cost or the card instructs you to trash itself. The VP gained from The Spice Must Flow's acquire effect remains even if you later trash that card.
answers.evidence: Trash from hand, discard or in play; “Reserve cards return to their Reserve stack”; optional except costs/self; FAQ says acquire VP “is retained if the card is later trashed.”

answers.answer: An acquire-box effect resolves once at the moment the card is acquired, not when later played. If you cannot draw because your deck is empty, reshuffle your discard pile into a new deck and continue. Persuasion not used during your Reveal turn is lost and cannot be carried forward.
answers.evidence: Acquire box effect occurs “at the moment you acquire”; reshuffle discard when deck empty; unused Persuasion “is lost.”

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and revealed during Reveal remain face up and in play until Clean Up, unless trashed first. Fremen Bond may use one or more other Fremen cards in play; two Bond cards may activate each other regardless of play order. They cease being in play at Clean Up when moved to discard.
answers.evidence: “Cards you play on Agent turns and reveal… remain face up and ‘in play’ until… Clean Up”; “two Fremen Bond cards can activate one another, regardless of order.”

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the Agent you just sent; the recalled Agent can be used again on a later Agent turn in the same round. A retreated troop goes from Conflict back to your garrison. “Retreat any number” can mean zero troops.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent returns “one of your other Agents”; can “use it again on another Agent turn in the same round”; retreat moves troop to garrison; FAQ says “any number” allows zero.

answers.answer: For a free-choice Influence effect that grants two, choose one Faction and gain both there; you cannot split the two across Factions. An Alliance icon requires you to hold that Faction's Alliance token. A minimum-Influence effect requires the specified minimum with that Faction.
answers.evidence: Free-choice gain-two: “you can't choose two different Factions”; Alliance icon “requires you to hold” token; some card effects require minimum Influence.

answers.answer: If the Alliance holder loses Influence after being tied, the formerly tied opponent takes the Alliance; if two opponents were tied, the former holder chooses which one receives it. If the holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4 or more, return the token to the board and the former holder loses its 1 VP.
answers.evidence: FAQ: previously tied opponent takes; “if several were tied, the former holder chooses its recipient”; at 3 or lower with nobody at 4+, token returns and old holder loses VP.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is revealed and used immediately that turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, when you draw five additional cards. A Plot Intrigue with a later Reveal effect stays face up until that effect is used, then is discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ: “Drawn during Reveal means immediately reveal and use this turn. Drawn after Reveal means keep it for next round”; Plot with later Reveal effect “stays face up until then, is used, then discarded.”

answers.answer: No. A “when you win a Conflict” Intrigue cannot be played after tying for first, because no one wins. If you receive such an Intrigue as a reward for an outright win, you may play it immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ: “‘When you win a Conflict’ Intrigues cannot be played after tying for first; if received as a winning reward they can be played immediately.”

answers.answer: If VP, spice, Solari, water, and garrisoned troops all tie, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed 12.
answers.evidence: FAQ: “If all four resource tiebreakers remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed the printed track’s 12.”

answers.answer: No. You must complete every held contract for that space with that one Agent placement; you cannot delay them to a later turn. They are another effect of that Agent turn and may resolve in any order with the space and Agent-box effects, provided you held them when placing the Agent.
answers.evidence: FAQ: “Fulfill all contracts you hold for the same space with one Agent placement”; completion is another effect that “can resolve in any order”; must hold at placement.

answers.answer: Shaddam does not begin with the set-aside Sardaukar contracts; they are not initially in his possession. With his Sardaukar Commander ability, when taking a contract he may choose a set-aside Sardaukar contract instead of a generally available one. His Emperor of the Known Universe restriction starts immediately when he plays Signet Ring to send an Agent and lasts for that turn only, not the full round.
answers.evidence: FAQ: Sardaukar contracts “do not start in your possession”; may choose one when acquiring contract; deployment restriction “takes effect immediately… lasts only for that turn.”

answers.answer: Feyd's token starts at the leftmost Training-track space and stays at the rightmost space once it reaches it. Lady Jessica begins with her Lady Jessica side face up, not Reverend Mother Jessica. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications state Feyd token placement and remaining at rightmost; “Lady Jessica… begin… Lady Jessica side face up”; FAQ says Reverend Mother Jessica may use ability on flip turn.

answers.answer: For Margot and Irulan, moving from 1 to 3 counts as reaching 2, so the effect triggers. It can trigger again later by losing Influence and then moving up through/reaching 2 again; descending through 2 does not count as reaching it. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild’s Favor from in play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding it from hand does.
answers.evidence: Clarification: you reach 2 moving past 2 with multiple Influence; can reach it again after losing and regaining, only when moving up; Guild's Favor Clean Up does not trigger discard ability.

answers.answer: Accept Contract uses the Spice Trade icon, has no cost, and always draws one card; with CHOAM it also takes a contract, while without CHOAM—or when no contracts remain—it gives 2 Solari instead. Dutiful Service uses the Emperor icon, has no cost, gains 1 Emperor Influence, and likewise takes a contract with CHOAM or 2 Solari without it/when none remain. Accept Contract is not a Faction and gives no automatic Influence; Dutiful Service gives one Emperor Influence once total (its listed effect is the same as the Faction advance, not an extra one).
answers.evidence: Board guide: Accept Contract is Spice Trade, no cost, always draw; CHOAM contract/otherwise 2 Solari. Dutiful Service is Emperor, gains 1 Emperor Influence and contract/otherwise 2 Solari. Faction clarification: Accept is non-Faction; Dutiful's one Influence counted once.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City icon, no cost, Combat space; visitor recruits one troop and draws one card, and the controller separately gains 1 Solari. Fremkit: Fremen icon, no cost, Combat space; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw a card. Research Station: City icon, costs 2 water, Combat space; recruit two troops and draw two cards.
answers.evidence: Board guide rows list Arrakeen City/Yes/no cost; Fremkit Fremen/Yes/no cost; Research Station City/Yes/2 water.

answers.answer: Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or two sandworms if you have Maker Hooks. Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or one sandworm if you have Hooks. Visiting either also gives all accumulated bonus spice, including when you choose worms. Hooks are retained and not spent when summoning.
answers.evidence: Board guide gives costs and base/worm options; Maker rules say a visit gains “all the bonus spice”; Hooks “are never spent to summon.”

answers.answer: Both Sietch Tabr choices require City access and 2+ Fremen Influence, with no resource entry cost. Option one: take Maker Hooks if you lack them, recruit one troop, and gain 1 water. Option two: gain 1 water and optionally remove the Shield Wall. The second choice gives no troop.
answers.evidence: Sietch Tabr row: “City… No resource cost; 2+ Fremen Influence”; choose Hooks + recruit + water, or water + optionally remove Wall.

answers.answer: High Council is a Landsraad, non-Combat space. Each visit costs 5 Solari. On your first visit, place your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and gain 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. Subsequent visits give 2 spice, draw an Intrigue, and recruit three troops.
answers.evidence: High Council row: Landsraad/No; 5 Solari each visit; first visit grants ongoing 2 Persuasion every Reveal; subsequent visit rewards listed.

answers.answer: Swordmaster costs 8 Solari before anyone gains one and 6 Solari once anyone has one. Each player may visit/gain the Swordmaster only once per game. The third Agent is available this round and for the rest of the game. A Rival obtaining Swordmaster also lowers the human cost to 6 Solari.
answers.evidence: Swordmaster row: “8 Solari before anyone gains Swordmaster; 6 once anyone has one”; once per player; available this round and rest of game; Rival gaining also reduces human cost.

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege uses Landsraad access; it requires 2+ Emperor Influence and costs 3 Solari. Its effects let you discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue, and recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It does not automatically give Emperor Influence and can recall only another Agent, not the one just placed.
answers.evidence: Imperial Privilege row: Landsraad; 3 Solari, 2+ Emperor; may discard Intrigue for one, recall one of your other Agents and draw; Landsraad is not a Faction.

answers.answer: Shipping uses Spice Trade access, requires 2+ Spacing Guild Influence, and costs 3 spice. It gives 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction, which need not be the Guild.
answers.evidence: Shipping row lists Spice Trade; 3 spice and 2+ Guild; “Gain 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction.”

answers.answer: Gather Support is Landsraad and not a Combat space: choose to pay 0 or 2 Solari; recruit two troops either way, and if you pay 2 also gain 1 water. Spice Refinery is City and a Combat space: choose to pay 0 or 1 spice; gain 2 Solari for free or 4 Solari if you pay 1 spice; its controller separately gains 1 Solari.
answers.evidence: Guide rows: Gather Support Landsraad/No with 0-or-2 Solari options; Spice Refinery City/Yes with 0-or-1 spice and 2-or-4 Solari, plus controller bonus.

answers.answer: Heighliner costs 5 spice, grants 1 Spacing Guild Influence and recruits five troops; it is a Combat space, so normal deployment is allowed. Desert Tactics costs 1 water, grants 1 Fremen Influence, recruits one troop, and optionally trashes a card; it is a Combat space. Sardaukar costs 4 spice, grants 1 Emperor Influence, draws an Intrigue and recruits four troops; it is not a Combat space, so normal deployment is not allowed there.
answers.evidence: Board guide lists Heighliner Guild/Yes/5 spice and five recruits; Desert Tactics Fremen/Yes/1 water, Influence, troop and optional trash; Sardaukar Emperor/No/4 spice, Influence, Intrigue, four troops.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall uses Landsraad access, has no entry cost and is non-Combat; draw an Intrigue, and if your Agent is there gain 1 Persuasion during your Reveal turn. Espionage uses Bene Gesserit access, costs 1 spice, is non-Combat, and gives 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, a card draw, and a Spy placement. Deliver Supplies uses Spacing Guild access, has no cost, is non-Combat, and gives 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.
answers.evidence: The three Board Space Guide rows list these icons, costs, Combat status and effects; Assembly Hall's Persuasion is conditional on Agent still being there at Reveal.

answers.answer: False Orders makes affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent's destination that turn. It may be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. Litany Against Fear's red box is ignored during Reveal, or when the card gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ: False Orders' affected opponents move Spy to an empty post “not connected to your Agent’s destination”; may play without an enemy Spy; Litany red box ignored in Reveal or normal Agent play.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the card removed by Manipulate. You may acquire it by other means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If it is still unacquired by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: FAQ: “opponents cannot acquire the removed card”; you may acquire by other means “without the 1-Persuasion discount”; otherwise remove at end of next Reveal.

answers.answer: The standard Rival starts with four cubes on the bottoms of Influence tracks, three troops in its garrison and the rest in supply, two Agents in supply with Swordmaster beside the board, three Spies, and 1 water; score and Combat markers start at 0. Shuffle House Hagal and put it near the Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card. The Rival is a scoring competitor: its 10+ VP can trigger Endgame and it can win.
answers.evidence: Rival setup specifies cubes, troops, Agents, Spies, water, score and Combat at 0; shuffle Hagal “retaining the 2P Reshuffle card”; its 10+ VP triggers Endgame “just like a human’s score.”

answers.answer: As soon as the Rival's count of Solari, spice, Intrigue cards and water (each counts as one) reaches its printed Swordmaster threshold, it spends that many resources and takes its third Agent, usable this round. If selecting payment, spend Solari first, then spice, then Intrigue cards, then water; keep any leftovers.
answers.evidence: Count resources together, “each unit counting as one”; at threshold spend that many and take third Agent; listed spending order and “keep leftovers”; usable in current round.

answers.answer: After Swordmaster, the Rival spends each exact set for 1 VP: 7 Solari, or 7 spice, or 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water. It cannot combine a mixed set of seven resources; the sets are resource-specific.
answers.evidence: “whenever it has 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water, spend each such set for 1 VP.”

answers.answer: The Rival chooses the Faction with least Influence and breaks ties by the leftmost priority icon. It gains the usual VP at 2 Influence and Alliance token VP like a human, but does not receive the resource bonus for reaching 4. A numbered Hagal Influence icon means the Faction in that position on the Rival's printed priority list.
answers.evidence: Rival “gains and loses Influence VP and Alliances like a human, but does not receive the resource bonus”; chooses least Influence, leftmost priority; numbered icon refers to position in priority list.

answers.answer: No. For a two-destination card, choose only the destination matching the current condition: Guild Influence selects between Accept Contract/Shipping, while Conflict tier selects between Deliver Supplies/Heighliner. If that selected destination is occupied, reveal a new Hagal card without using the other destination.
answers.evidence: “With a two-destination card, select only the destination matching the current conditions (Guild Influence…; Conflict tier…); if that destination is occupied, reveal a new card, without using the other destination.”

answers.answer: Yes. At every Combat space the Rival deploys up to two available garrison troops even if the card recruited none. Troops recruited at a non-Combat space go into its garrison, not the Conflict. A conditional 2+ Influence bonus not met is simply omitted; it does not prevent placing the Agent.
answers.evidence: “At every Combat space also deploy up to two available troops from garrison, even when the card recruited none”; elsewhere recruits to garrison; unmet 2+ bonus “never prevents placing the Agent.”

answers.answer: Without a specified post type, the Rival uses the first available Faction observation post in its priority order; if all four are occupied, it ignores placement. Placing its third and final supply Spy immediately recalls its other two and triggers its Scheme. The Rival never recalls Spies for Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Unspecified post: first available Faction post in priority order; all four occupied means ignore; placing final Spy recalls other two and triggers Scheme; Rival never uses Infiltrate/Gather.

answers.answer: If the Scheme recruits troops before Agent placement and the Rival then visits a Combat space on that turn, those Scheme-recruited troops deploy too. If a Place Spy card finds no legal post, ignore placement, reveal another Hagal card, and continue the Agent turn.
answers.evidence: “If a Scheme recruits troops before Agent placement… deploy those troops too”; Place Spy without available post: ignore and “immediately reveal another Hagal card and continue.”

answers.answer: At Hagga Basin or Deep Desert, the Rival always takes all accumulated bonus spice. With Hooks and a Conflict that permits worms, it summons one at Hagga or two at Deep Desert instead of base spice; if it summons none, it takes the base 2 or 4 spice. Without Hooks, or if the Conflict is protected by the Shield Wall, it cannot summon and takes base spice; Imperial Basin always provides 1 base spice. The Maker-space visit still collects the accumulated bonus spice in every case.
answers.evidence: Rival always collects all bonus spice; with Hooks and permitted Conflict, summons one/two instead of base; “If it summons none, take… base spice”; Imperial Basin always 1.

answers.answer: At the beginning of Combat, if the Rival has at least one deployed unit, reveal a Hagal card in turn order and add its bottom swords to strength. If Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. Then humans have their normal Combat Intrigue window and may respond. A unit-free Rival gets no Hagal strength bonus.
answers.evidence: Combat: “if the Rival has at least one unit deployed”; reveal Hagal and add bottom swords; Reshuffle means reshuffle/reveal again; “Humans then have their normal Combat Intrigue window.”

answers.answer: Yes: the Rival gains control bonuses and defensive troops, wins Conflict cards and battle-icon VP normally, and doubles rewards when it has a sandworm. It always takes optional Conflict VP if it can pay the resources or recall required Spies. It never takes contracts; a contract reward gives it 2 Solari even with CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Rival “gains control bonuses… defensive troop… battle-icon VP… doubles rewards”; always take optional Conflict VP if able; “never takes contracts… gives it 2 Solari, even with CHOAM.”

answers.answer: During Reveal effect resolution, total and announce strength and set the Combat marker at any point; you may update it as needed during that turn. If strength exceeds 20, flip the marker to its +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Reveal: total strength and set marker “at any point while resolving, updating it as needed”; over 20, “flip the marker to the +20 side and start again.”

answers.answer: A Leader's Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring on one of your Agent turns; merely revealing it on a Reveal turn does not activate it. Card text can override the usual game rules.
answers.evidence: Signet Ring ability “activates when you play your Signet Ring card on one of your Agent turns, not merely when you reveal it”; “Cards of any type can override the usual rules.”

answers.answer: A Recall Spy icon returns one of your Spies from an observation post to your supply, usually as a cost for a powerful effect. It does not automatically perform Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those are separate recalls for their stated effects.
answers.evidence: Recall Spy icon “returns one of your Spies from a post to your supply (usually as a cost for a powerful effect)”; separate no-card effects are Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence.

answers.answer: The specific trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. An ordinary discard instruction discards a card of your choice from your hand but cannot discard an Intrigue unless it specifies one; discard is not trashing.
answers.evidence: “separate trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand”; ordinary discard is from hand and Intrigue excluded unless specified.

answers.answer: Yes. A doubled reward that grants 1 Influence of your choice gives two Influence gains, and the reward example allows them to be with the same Faction or two different Factions. By contrast, a single effect saying gain two free-choice Influence requires choosing one Faction for both; it cannot be split.
answers.evidence: Doubled reward example gives 2 Influence “with the same Faction or two different Factions”; free-choice gain-two icon cannot choose two different Factions.

answers.answer: Resolve the Rival's printed Signet Ring effect/ability as directed by its Rival card. It does not require a human Signet Ring card or a Reveal turn: Hagal effects, including Signet Ring, are applied during the Rival's Agent-turn procedure.
answers.evidence: Rival follows its printed Signet Ring and Scheme abilities; apply Hagal effects. The Rival “never takes a Reveal turn.”

answers.answer: The Rival uses its own Hooks. A Maker Hooks icon gives it one token from the bank only if it lacks one; if it already has Hooks, it takes no second token. Shield Wall removal works only if it has Hooks and the Wall remains; without Hooks it is ignored, and if the Wall is already gone there is no further effect.
answers.evidence: Rival Hooks and Wall table specifies no Hooks → take token; already has Hooks → no second; removal only with Hooks and Wall present; otherwise ignore/no effect.

answers.answer: Secrets uses Bene Gesserit access, has no entry cost, and is not a Combat space. It gives 1 Bene Gesserit Influence and draws an Intrigue from the Intrigue Deck. Separately, each opponent holding at least four Intrigues gives you one chosen at random from their hand/supply of Intrigues.
answers.evidence: Secrets row: Bene Gesserit/No cost/No Combat; gain 1 Influence and draw Intrigue; each opponent with 4+ gives one selected at random.

answers.answer: Imperial Basin uses Spice Trade access, has no entry cost, and is a Combat space. The visitor gets 1 base spice plus all bonus spice at the space. The controller separately gets 1 spice whenever anyone visits; if visitor and controller are the same player, that player receives the controller's extra 1 spice too.
answers.evidence: Imperial Basin row: Spice Trade/Yes/no cost; visitor “1 base spice plus all bonus spice; controller gains 1 spice.” Controlled-location clarification says resolve visitor and controller effects even if same player.

answers.answer: At Round Start, reveal the new Conflict face up next to the deck, on top of any Conflict cards left from earlier rounds; the old unclaimed card remains. Each player draws five hand cards after the new Conflict is revealed.
answers.evidence: “Reveal a new Conflict card… place it face up next to the deck (on top of any Conflict cards remaining from previous rounds). Then each player draws five cards.”

answers.answer: Each human places one cube at the bottom of each of the four Faction Influence tracks; none begins holding an Alliance, since all four Alliance tokens start on their marked track areas. The Shield Wall token starts on its marked area below Spice Refinery, so the Wall is present.
answers.evidence: Setup: place Alliance tokens on marked areas of four Influence tracks; each player puts cubes on bottom spaces; Shield Wall token on marked area below Spice Refinery.

answers.answer: In 3–4 player play, the player with the First Player marker takes the first turn, then turns proceed clockwise. A player who Reveals skips their remaining turns; Player Turns end once every player has Revealed. Combat Intrigue priority starts with First Player and proceeds clockwise. Each eligible player with a unit may play any number of Combat Intrigues before passing; the window resolves when all involved players pass consecutively.
answers.evidence: Players proceed “starting with the First Player… clockwise”; after Reveal turns are skipped, phase ends when all Revealed; Combat Intrigue starts First Player clockwise and players may play “any number”; resolution after consecutive passes.

answers.answer: The steps are: Reveal Cards (reveal remaining hand), Resolve Reveal Effects (gain the revealed cards' Reveal boxes, in any order), and Clean Up (move all cards in front of you to discard). The player chooses the order of Reveal effects; they need not follow card order.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn has three steps in order; effects may be gained “in any order.”

answers.answer: Shuffle each human's 10-card starting deck and put it face down in their supply left of the Leader. Without CHOAM, omit CHOAM cards, then shuffle the Intrigue and Imperium decks separately face down; deal five Imperium cards face up into the Row; keep Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow in separate Reserve stacks. Each human's Combat marker starts at 0, all three Spies and the Councilor start in supply, and Control markers remain in supply.
answers.evidence: Setup and Initial card states describe shuffled face-down human deck, decks, five-card Row and separate Reserve stacks; components put in supply; Combat marker at 0.

answers.answer: With Persuasion you may ordinarily acquire any of the five Imperium Row cards or either Reserve card, Prepare the Way or The Spice Must Flow. Each card's cost is shown at its top right. These purchases are made during your Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: “During your Reveal turn, use Persuasion to acquire any of the five cards in the Imperium Row, or Prepare the Way or The Spice Must Flow”; cost is at top right.

answers.answer: Yes. Ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional, so you may decline even when a legal action exists. Shield Wall detonation is also optional (“may remove” the token). Once removed, the Wall returns to the box and cannot return later in the game.
answers.evidence: “Ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional”; when Shield Wall detonation appears “you may remove” it; “gone for the rest of the game and cannot return.”

answers.answer: The played card must have an Agent icon matching the destination's access icon, unless the card has a Spy Agent icon and you have a Spy at a connected post. Having a connected Spy alone does not let a card with only City access enter Shipping; Infiltrate bypasses occupancy, not the icon requirement. If the card actually has the Spy Agent icon, it can send the Agent to any space connected to a post where your Spy is present without recalling that Spy.
answers.evidence: Agent-turn rule requires a matching icon; Spy section: a connected Spy alone does not give all cards Spy-Agent access; Spy Agent icon provides access to connected space and does not recall Spy.

answers.answer: Yes. You may play a legal Plot Intrigue before placing the Agent; resources it grants before entry join your available supply and can pay the entry cost. Resources from the Agent card used to place the Agent, or from the destination, arrive only after placement and cannot pay that same entry cost.
answers.evidence: On Agent turn, Plot before placement may grant entry resources; effects “only after placement” from destination or played Agent card cannot pay for same entry.

answers.answer: No. In two-player play, after both humans Reveal, continue the Rival's Agent turns while it has Agents in supply. Move to Combat only after both humans have Revealed and the Rival has used all its Agents. The Rival never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: In two-player play, skip humans who Revealed but continue Rival turns; Combat once both humans Revealed and Rival used all Agents; “Rival never Reveals.”

answers.evidence: The “Board Space Guide — Standard 2–4 Players” table lists all 22 spaces with Agent access icon and explicit Combat? column.

answers.answer: When a Conflict is revealed for a location the human already controls, its controller may deploy one troop from their supply directly to the Conflict; it is optional and requires no Agent visit. After Combat rewards, all Combat markers reset to 0 before Makers begins.
answers.evidence: Round Start resolves defensive troop bonus “for a location already controlled when its Conflict is revealed”; controller “may” deploy from supply without Agent visit; after rewards “all Combat markers reset to 0.”

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up in front of you, then move one Agent from your Leader to an unoccupied matching board space. Resolve that card's Agent box and ignore its Reveal box. You cannot reuse a card already in play or in your discard pile for this turn, nor simply move an Agent already on the board; the described action uses a hand card and an Agent from the Leader.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: “Play one card from your hand face up”; send an Agent “from your Leader” to unoccupied matching space; gain Agent-box effects and ignore Reveal box.

answers.answer: The restriction applies immediately when Shaddam plays Signet Ring to send an Agent; he cannot postpone it by choosing to resolve board-space effects first. General freedom to order effects does not delay this Leader restriction.
answers.evidence: Shaddam clarification: restriction “takes effect immediately” when playing Signet Ring to send Agent; “general freedom to order… effects cannot postpone it.”

answers.answer: In four-player play with four different positive strengths, first, second, and third place each receive the corresponding printed reward; fourth receives no reward. The highest-strength player wins and takes the Conflict card face up, then checks it for a mandatory battle-icon match.
answers.evidence: With four players, ordinary first, second and third receive rewards; winner is highest and takes first reward; winner's card steps take it face up then check matching icon.

answers.answer: Players may choose a Leader or select one at random; random distribution is not required.
answers.evidence: Setup says each player takes a Leader “(choose, or select at random).”

answers.answer: An ordinary draw-a-card effect draws from your own deck. You do not choose directly from your discard pile; if your deck is empty, shuffle the discard pile into a new deck and continue drawing.
answers.evidence: “An ordinary draw-a-card effect draws from your own deck”; empty deck triggers shuffle of discard, not direct choice.

answers.answer: Shuffle the House Hagal deck and place it near the shared Rival; retain the 2P Reshuffle card in the deck rather than removing it.
answers.evidence: Rival setup: “Shuffle House Hagal and place the deck near the shared Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card.”

answers.answer: All four Maker Hooks tokens start in the common bank; normal setup assigns none to a human player. When acquired, a token moves from the bank onto that player's garrison.
answers.evidence: “Put all 4 Maker Hooks tokens in this common bank; normal setup assigns none to a human player”; acquired token moves onto player's garrison.

answers.answer: Yes. If Combat Intrigue changes a participant's deployed units or strength, update their Combat marker when that card resolves during the Combat Intrigue window. The adjusted strength shown on the track when the window ends is used to resolve rewards; Reveal strength is not fixed through cleanup.
answers.evidence: If a Combat Intrigue changes units/strength, “adjust their Combat marker when that card resolves”; Reveal total “is not fixed for the rest of the round”; use adjusted strength.

answers.answer: Gain Solari, spice, and water from the common bank. You do not take gained resources from another player's supply; when paying those resources, return them to the bank.
answers.evidence: “Whenever you gain Solari, spice or water, take it from the bank; whenever you pay any of these resources, return it to the bank.”

answers.answer: Shuffle all 20 standard contracts face down, then expose two face up as the offers and leave the remaining 18 face down in the bank. Since the stack is shuffled first, players do not choose the initial offers or preset the bank's order.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup says “Shuffle the 20 contracts face down, then flip two face up… place the remaining 18 face down in the bank.”
